newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures surge at close, tone fragile.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures surge at close, tone fragile.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures extended their gains to end sharply on Monday, but dealers said the rise was not backed by substantial volume and could prove unsustainable.
After opening 100 points above its Friday close, the lead Nikkei 225 September contract made further headway, adding 435 points to end at 20,265 on volume of 15,265 lots.
"It was basically a technical rebound. The market gapped up at the open and then went up on quite thin volume," a trader with a Japanese brokerage said.
He said the September Nikkei rose from 20,050 to 20,200 on volume of less than 2,000 lots.
"People were chasing high-tech shares on the cash market, like what happened on Wall Street on Friday," he said, adding that this had spurred short-covering of Nikkei futures.
He said the lead contract faced immediate resistance around the 20,290 level, with a stronger barrier expected above 20,400.
Dealers said the yen's slightly weaker tone and comments by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita about Japan's economic recovery helped underpin the market.
Matsushita said Japan's economy remained on a gradual recovery trend despite lingering impact from the increase in the consumption tax on April 1.
On Taiwan futures, the July contract added 4.4 points to end at 408.5 on volume of 966 lots.
